title: Real Quadratic Fields: The First Open Case of Hilbert's 12th
content: Hilbert's 12th problem (Kronecker's *Jugendtraum*) seeks explicit generators of the abelian extensions of a number field K. It is solved for K = ℚ (Kronecker–Weber: roots of unity) and for imaginary quadratic K (complex multiplication: singular moduli and elliptic units). The first genuinely open case is the family of **real quadratic fields** ℚ(√d), d > 0. The distinction from the imaginary quadratic case is unit-theoretic: an imaginary quadratic field has unit rank 0 (its units are just roots of unity), while a real quadratic field has unit rank 1 — an infinite unit group generated by a fundamental unit. It is precisely this infinite unit and the transcendence of its logarithm that put real quadratic fields into the domain of the Stark conjectures rather than the classical CM theory.
mathContext: A real quadratic field is a totally real number field of degree 2. Signature $(r_1, r_2) = (2, 0)$, unit rank $r_1 + r_2 - 1 = 1$; the imaginary quadratic case has $(0,1)$ and rank $0$.

title: Two Infinite Places (Totally Real, Degree 2)
content: `card_infinitePlace_eq_two`: a totally real degree-2 field has exactly two infinite places, both real. The proof feeds three facts to `omega`: total reality gives nrComplexPlaces K = 0 (`nrComplexPlaces_eq_zero_iff`), the count splits as #(InfinitePlace K) = nrReal + nrComplex (`card_eq_nrRealPlaces_add_nrComplexPlaces`), and the signature identity nrReal + 2·nrComplex = [K : ℚ] = 2 (`card_add_two_mul_card_eq_rank`). Together these force nrReal = 2, nrComplex = 0, and #(InfinitePlace K) = 2.
prerequisites: infinite places of a number field

title: Unit Rank One — The Source of the Stark Unit
content: `rank_eq_one`: a totally real degree-2 field (an abstract real quadratic field) has unit rank 1. Since Dirichlet's unit theorem gives rank K = #(InfinitePlace K) − 1 and the field has two infinite places, `rw [rank]; omega` yields rank 1. This is the crux of the whole story: unit rank 1 means the unit group is ℤ × (roots of unity), so there is a fundamental unit ε of infinite order. That ε is the Stark unit, and its very existence is what makes the real quadratic case belong to the Stark conjectures rather than to CM theory.
mathContext: $\mathrm{rank}\,K = \#(\mathrm{InfinitePlace}\,K) - 1 = 2 - 1 = 1$; the unit group is $\mathbb{Z} \times \mu_K$ with fundamental unit $\varepsilon$.
prerequisites: unit group of a number field

title: The Imaginary Quadratic Complement — Rank Zero
content: `rank_eq_zero_of_not_isTotallyReal`: a degree-2 field that is *not* totally real is imaginary quadratic and has unit rank 0. Non-total-reality gives nrComplexPlaces K ≠ 0 (contrapositive of `nrComplexPlaces_eq_zero_iff`); with the signature identity nrReal + 2·nrComplex = 2 this forces nrComplex = 1, nrReal = 0, hence a single infinite place and rank 0 (`omega`). Up to roots of unity such a field has no nontrivial units — exactly the CM-solved case of Hilbert's 12th, and the rank drop from 1 to 0 is precisely why it is easier than the real quadratic case.

title: The Dichotomy: rank = 1 ⟺ Totally Real
content: `rank_eq_one_iff_isTotallyReal`: among degree-2 number fields, unit rank 1 holds *exactly when* the field is totally real. This packages the real/imaginary split into a single equivalence: real quadratic (totally real) ⟺ rank 1 (the open Hilbert-12 case), and its complement is imaginary quadratic ⟺ rank 0 (CM-solved). The forward direction is a `by_contra` reducing to `rank_eq_zero_of_not_isTotallyReal` (rank cannot be both 1 and 0); the backward direction is `rank_eq_one`. The equivalence makes explicit that the arithmetic difficulty tracks the unit rank, not the degree.
mathContext: For $[K:\mathbb{Q}] = 2$: $\mathrm{rank}\,K = 1 \iff K \text{ totally real}$ (real quadratic); otherwise $\mathrm{rank}\,K = 0$ (imaginary quadratic).

title: Regulator = A Single Bare Logarithm (No Multiplicity)
content: `regulator_eq_single_log`: for a totally real degree-2 field the regulator equals |log w(ε)| — a single archimedean logarithm of the fundamental (Stark) unit ε, with **no** multiplicity factor. The proof reproves the rank-one collapse inline (keeping the file self-contained): since rank K = 1, `Fin (rank K)` is a singleton, so transporting the `Unique` instance along `equivFinRank` makes the place index type a singleton and `Matrix.det_unique` reduces `regulator_eq_det` to its single 1×1 entry mult(w)·|log w(ε)|; then `IsTotallyReal.mult_eq` (mult w = 1 at a real place) strips the multiplicity, leaving the bare logarithm. This sharpens the general rank-one collapse (sibling oq-02), where a mixed-signature cubic's complex place contributes a factor of 2.
mathContext: $R_K = |\log w(\varepsilon)|$ (real quadratic), sharper than the general $R_K = \mathrm{mult}(w)\,|\log w(\varepsilon)|$ because $\mathrm{mult}(w) = 1$ at a real place.
prerequisites: the regulator as a determinant of logarithms
